domain_label: Sweater Vertical — Landed-Cost Stack, Duty Reality & COGS-to-Stock Banding
purpose: A method for converting T4's ex-factory per-article bands (A1 cotton-blend core, A2 fine-acrylic value, A3 merino/lambswool premium) into honest landed COGS-to-stock at the California (Turlock) receiving door, by stacking the correct HTS heading-6110 MFN duty trio (cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% [FACT], wool 6110.11 ~16% [FACT], acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% [FACT]) plus the volatile India surcharge, ocean/air freight, MPF/HMF, broker/bond/drayage and the post-de-minimis bulk-Importer-of-Record operating model, while never hardening a [UNKNOWN] forward surcharge or the inherited [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate into a fake-precise quote.
assumptions: the three MFN ad-valorem duty rates are cited public facts (cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5%, wool 6110.11 ~16%, acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% [FACT-USITC]); the prior 'cotton ~7%' figure is a corrected upstream error and is never used

duty is levied on the ex-factory (~FOB transaction) value, not the freight-inflated value, with separately-stated international freight excluded [FACT-US customs valuation]; freight and fees are added after duty, not multiplied by the duty rate
ex-factory bands are inherited from T4 as labelled estimates whose width is set by the [UNKNOWN] Ludhiana knit+LINK job-work rate (A1 ~$4-9, A2 ~$3.5-8, A3 ~$6-22+); they are not re-derived here

the India surcharge rides additively on MFN (total duty = MFN + surcharge), is fibre-blind, and is modelled as a 0-15% band central ~10% [FACT current] plus an explicit 25-50% spike scenario [FACT that the 50% peak was realised Aug-2025]; the forward level is a genuine [UNKNOWN]

de-minimis (Section 321, <$800) is repealed for all countries effective Aug 29, 2025 (EO 14324) [FACT-dated], so the operating model is bulk Importer-of-Record to a California 3PL to domestic ship, not ship-direct-per-order; the ~$651.50 MPF cap reinforces this
all landed dollar bands are estimates, never claims of an actual paid invoice; every duty/legal/dated claim is tagged [FACT], [ESTIMATE] with method+basis+confidence, or [UNKNOWN]
exclusions: re-deriving the ex-factory conversion cost (that is T4's mfg_economics segment; this segment accepts its bands as input)
the contribution-margin-after-CAC P&L, CAC, returns, repeat and break-even (those are the demand-side unit-economics segment and the analyst-B/analyst-C spine; this KB stops at landed COGS-to-stock)
asserting a single forward India surcharge level as a forecast, or hardening the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate or any trade fragment into a quotable per-unit number
the make-vs-buy boundary, yarn sourcing, machine selection and finishing (T2/T3/T4/T6 own those upstream)
tax, customs-brokerage or trade-law advice for a specific filing; this models the landed-cost stack and its decisions, not an actual entry

competency_questions.question: What is the correct MFN duty trio on heading-6110 sweaters by fibre, and why does it re-rank the line at the border versus the factory gate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HTS_FIBRE_CLASSIFICATION names heading 6110 and the three sub-lines, MFN_DUTY_TRIO states cotton ~16.5% / wool ~16% / acrylic-MMF ~32% as [FACT-USITC] with the corrected (not ~7%) cotton rate, and LANDED_RERANKING shows the 32% MMF wall flipping factory-gate A2<A1<A3 into landed A1~=A2<A3

competency_questions.question: How is landed cost computed from an ex-factory band, and does the formula recompute consistently?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DUTY_FORMULA computes duty $ = ex-factory x (MFN + surcharge) on the transaction value, and LANDED_COST_FORMULA stacks ex-factory x (1 + duty% + surcharge%) + freight + MPF/HMF + broker/bond/drayage = landed, with the stated inputs recomputing to the A1/A2/A3 landed bands

competency_questions.question: Why is de-minimis repeal a model-flip rather than a marginal cost, and what operating model replaces ship-direct?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMINIMIS_REPEAL states EO 14324 effective Aug 29 2025 ending the <$800 duty-free shield for India, and IOR_3PL_MODEL establishes the bulk Importer-of-Record to California 3PL to domestic ship default, reinforced by the MPF cap and fee structure

competency_questions.question: How is the volatile India surcharge modelled honestly given its history and forward uncertainty?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INDIA_SURCHARGE_BAND states the additive-on-MFN mechanism, the current ~10% Section-122 baseline [FACT], the realised 50% Aug-2025 peak [FACT] and the [UNKNOWN] forward with the ~Jul-2026 sunset and Section-301 risk, and SURCHARGE_SPIKE_SCENARIO supplies the 25-50% stress case

competency_questions.question: Why does the fee structure alone reward bulk and punish per-order, independent of duty?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MPF_HMF_FEES states the 0.3464% MPF with $33.58 floor / $651.50 cap and the 0.125% ocean-only HMF, and BROKER_BOND_DRAYAGE states the per-entry broker/ISF/bond costs that amortise over a bulk entry but dominate per tiny parcel

competency_questions.question: How does the inbound freight line behave, and what is the right mode at launch versus maturity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OCEAN_AIR_FREIGHT presents freight as a volume curve (FCL ~$0.5-1.5, LCL ~$1-6 + fixed drag, air ~$1.5-6 sample-only) and names LCL at launch / FCL at maturity, flagging air-per-order as the dead de-minimis route

competency_questions.question: Why is the chief-weight blend ratio a tariff switch, and what IOR liability does it create?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHIEF_WEIGHT_CLIFF states that classification follows fibre of chief weight by mass, that flipping past 50% MMF nearly doubles duty (16.5% to 32%), and that the brand-as-IOR owns the mis-declaration liability, requiring blend % + tolerance + a fibre-composition check in every PO

competency_questions.question: What is the landed band for each of the three articles, and why is each band that wide?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: A1_COTTON_LANDED ~$6-14, A2_ACRYLIC_LANDED ~$6-14 and A3_MERINO_LANDED ~$9-31+ each state their MFN rate, surcharge, freight/fees and the [UNKNOWN]-knit+LINK + surcharge volatility driving the width, with band-centre points flagged [DOWNGRADED] illustrations

competency_questions.question: Why does acrylic's factory-gate cost lead not survive the US border?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: A2_ACRYLIC_LANDED and LANDED_RERANKING show the ~32% MMF duty adding ~$1 over cotton's ~$0.99 on a same-priced garment, eating acrylic's ~$0.5-1 ex-factory saving so A1 and A2 land in the same ~$6-14 band

competency_questions.question: What working-capital reality does the mandatory bulk-import model impose, and how is it carried not double-counted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WORKING_CAPITAL_INHERIT states that bulk IOR pre-commits inventory cash (dye-lot MOQ + ocean lead time) carried from T4, named as a cash-cycle kill-risk feeding the decision brain, not added as a per-unit COGS line

competency_questions.question: What legal exposure must the landed-cost work flag honestly and not wave through?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEGAL_DUTY_PUBLICITY states the duty-misclassification/blend-drift IOR liability and the HIGH right-of-publicity/Lanham false-endorsement exposure (athlete/celebrity names = Cal. Civ. Code 3344/3344.1 + Lanham 43(a)), both kept as binding flags

competency_questions.question: How is honesty discipline enforced across the landed bands so direction is trusted but level is not over-read?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONESTY_LEDGER separates the [FACT] duty/de-minimis/MPF/HMF anchors from the [ESTIMATE] landed bands and the [UNKNOWN] forward surcharge + knit+LINK rate, and flags the single-point landed figures as [DOWNGRADED] band-centre illustrations

competency_questions.question: What does the landed-cost segment hand to the contribution/decision layer, and what stays out of scope?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LANDED_HANDOFF delivers landed COGS-to-stock per article with its surcharge stress range and explicitly stops before CAC/returns/contribution, naming the decision-brain dependencies (re-confirm surcharge per PO, fund the cash cycle, hold the blend tolerance)

glossary.definition: The true per-unit cost at the US (Turlock) receiving door = ex-factory (~FOB) value + ocean/air freight + insurance + US duty (MFN + India surcharge) + MPF/HMF + broker/bond/ISF/drayage; it becomes the COGS-to-stock that the downstream contribution P&L is read against, and is the whole output of this segment.

The three cited ad-valorem rates on heading-6110 sweaters by fibre of chief weight: cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% [FACT], wool 6110.11 ~16% [FACT], acrylic/man-made-fibre 6110.30.30 ~32% [FACT-USITC]; the corrected figures, with cotton ~16.5% (never the discredited ~7%) and acrylic the ~2x outlier.

A country-specific US surcharge layered additively on top of MFN for India (total duty = MFN base + surcharge, both on entered value), fibre-blind, modelled as a 0-15% band central ~10% Section-122 [FACT current] plus a 25-50% spike scenario [FACT the 50% peak was realised Aug-2025]; the forward level is [UNKNOWN] with a ~Jul-2026 Section-122 sunset and a pending Section-301 risk.

The Aug 29, 2025 [FACT-dated] suspension of the Section 321 <$800 duty-free exemption for all countries including India, which kills the ship-direct-per-order model and forces a bulk Importer-of-Record to California 3PL to domestic ship operation; every parcel is now dutiable with no $800 shield.

The chief-weight-by-mass classification rule: a 55/45 cotton-acrylic garment is 'cotton' at ~16.5%, but flip to 55% acrylic and the same sweater becomes MMF at ~32%, nearly doubling duty; as Importer of Record the brand owns this liability, so blend % + tolerance + a fibre-composition check belong in every PO.

Merchandise Processing Fee 0.3464% of entered value with a $33.58 floor and $651.50 cap per formal entry [FACT-CBP], and Harbor Maintenance Fee 0.125% of cargo value, ocean-only, no cap [FACT]; the MPF cap is the whole bulk-versus-per-order story, hitting ~$0.13-0.65/garment at bulk versus the $33.58 floor on a single parcel.

The legally liable party (the brand) filing the customs entry and owing duty and classification compliance; under the post-de-minimis bulk model the brand is IOR, paying duty once on a bulk entry, capping MPF, amortising freight, and carrying the blend-drift mis-declaration liability.

Per-unit inbound freight falls in steps with volume, not a single number: ocean FCL ~$0.5-1.5/garment at maturity, ocean LCL ~$1-6 plus fixed CFS/doc/ISF drag at first small bulk runs, air ~$1.5-6/garment for samples/PPS only; the per-order air-from-India route (the dead de-minimis model) is ~$3-6/garment of freight alone before any duty.

The headline finding that the ~32% MMF duty inverts the factory-gate order A2<A1<A3 into the landed order A1~=A2<A3: acrylic's ~$0.5-1 ex-factory cost lead over cotton is almost exactly eaten by ~$1 of extra duty, so A1 and A2 sit in the same ~$6-14 landed band and cotton becomes the duty-friendly anchor [FACT on rates; arithmetic on the inversion].

A single-point landed figure (A1 ~$11, A2 ~$11, A3 ~$20) that reads more precise than the evidence supports because both the ex-factory band (blocked by the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate) and the surcharge are volatile; used as a planning anchor robust in direction, soft in level, never quoted as a measured COGS.

nodes.definition: Accept T4's per-article ex-factory conversion bands as the input level this segment stacks the import chain on top of, without re-deriving them: A1 cotton-blend core ~$4-9, A2 fine-acrylic value ~$3.5-8, A3 merino/lambswool premium ~$6-22+ per garment, all labelled [ESTIMATE] whose width is set by the single [UNKNOWN] Ludhiana knit+LINK job-work rate (the dominant uncertainty inside the whole landed stack). Duty applies to this ~FOB transaction value, not the freight-inflated value, so this band both sets the level of the landed stack and propagates its uncertainty into every downstream landed band.

included: the three ex-factory bands as accepted input
the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate as the inherited width driver
duty applying to the ex-factory transaction value

pros.claim: Taking T4's bands as a labelled input keeps the landed model honest about where its uncertainty originates instead of inventing a tighter ex-factory number
pros.example: carrying A3 ~$6-22+ as order-of-magnitude rather than a point makes the wide A3 landed band traceable to the upstream [UNKNOWN], not to sloppiness

cons.claim: Inheriting a wide ex-factory band caps how tight any landed band can be, so precision is blocked one layer up
cons.example: no freight or duty refinement can narrow A3 landed while its ex-factory yarn cost stays a stale single anchor

failure_modes: treating the band-centre ex-factory point as a measured cost and propagating false precision into landed
re-deriving ex-factory here and double-counting T4's work
acceptance_tests: the three ex-factory bands are stated as accepted [ESTIMATE] input with the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate named as the width driver, and duty is noted to apply to the ex-factory transaction value
revisit_triggers: a live Ludhiana knit+LINK job-work quote lands and halves the ex-factory band
T4 republishes the ex-factory bands
an importer quote fixes the A3 premium-yarn cost

base.update_signal: the ex-factory band or the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate is updated

nodes.definition: Establish the classification spine: sweaters/pullovers/cardigans fall under HTS heading 6110, and the duty line is set by the fibre of chief weight by mass into three sub-lines used throughout this KB: cotton 6110.20.20, wool 6110.11.00, and acrylic/man-made-fibre 6110.30.30 [FACT-USITC/CBP ruling N272437 on the MMF line]. India gets no FTA preference on heading 6110 (the 'Free' special-rate column lists Australia, Korea, Israel etc., not India) [FACT-USITC special-rate column], so there is no tariff shortcut by virtue of sourcing in India. The exact 10-digit suffix per article is [UNKNOWN] until the tech pack fixes fibre % and value.

included: heading 6110 and the three fibre sub-lines
chief-weight-by-mass as the classifier
no India FTA preference on 6110

pros.claim: Fixing the heading and the three sub-lines first gives every downstream duty number a citeable HTS anchor
pros.example: tagging A2 to 6110.30.30 makes its 32% MMF rate traceable to a specific line, not a guess

cons.claim: The exact 10-digit suffix is [UNKNOWN] until the tech pack fixes fibre % and value, so the precise duty line carries residual uncertainty
cons.example: an A3 wool value-break or an A1/A2 chief-weight call could shift the precise suffix

failure_modes: assuming India enjoys an FTA-free rate on 6110 when the special-rate column excludes it
treating the 6-digit heading as fixing duty when the chief-weight fibre call still governs
acceptance_tests: heading 6110 and the cotton/wool/MMF sub-lines are stated with chief-weight-by-mass as the classifier and the no-India-FTA-preference fact
revisit_triggers: a tech pack fixes the fibre % and value, setting the 10-digit suffix
a US-India trade deal adds a 6110 carve-out or preference
a CBP classification ruling on a specific blend lands

base.update_signal: a fibre-composition fix or a 6110 preference change occurs

nodes.definition: State the correct MFN ad-valorem duty trio and its consequence: cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% [FACT-USITC], wool 6110.11 ~16% [FACT-USITC], acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% [FACT-USITC] - the highest, roughly 2x the others. The prior 'cotton ~7%' figure is a corrected upstream error and is never used: sweaters of cotton are 16.5%, more than double what the original plan assumed, so every upstream margin model using ~7% must be corrected up. The 32% MMF wall on acrylic is the headline of the whole landed analysis: it is what erases acrylic's factory-gate cost lead at the border. Duty is a percentage on the ex-factory value, so it scales with both fibre and cost.

included: the three corrected MFN rates as [FACT]
the ~7% cotton error correction
the 32% MMF wall as the headline driver
excluded: the India surcharge layered on top (INDIA_SURCHARGE_BAND)

pros.claim: Carrying the corrected 16.5/16/32 trio prevents every downstream margin model from inheriting the discredited ~7% cotton figure
pros.example: an A1 landed band built on 16.5% rather than 7% roughly doubles the duty line and corrects the upstream optimism

cons.claim: Stating rates as point figures can read more fixed than reality when surcharge and exact suffix still move the all-in number
cons.example: the ~16.5% cotton base is firm but the all-in cotton duty swings with the [UNKNOWN] surcharge

failure_modes: reviving the corrected-away ~7% cotton figure in a downstream model
reading the MFN base as the all-in duty and omitting the additive surcharge
acceptance_tests: cotton ~16.5%, wool ~16%, acrylic/MMF ~32% are stated as [FACT-USITC] with the ~7% correction noted and the 32% MMF wall flagged as the headline
revisit_triggers: USITC revises a heading-6110 MFN rate
a CBP ruling reclassifies an article's fibre line
an upstream model is found still using the ~7% cotton figure

base.update_signal: an MFN duty rate or a fibre classification changes

nodes.definition: Establish the structural fact that flips the operating model: Executive Order 14324 (signed Jul 30, 2025) suspended duty-free de-minimis (Section 321, 19 USC 1321, formerly <$800 duty-free per person per day) for ALL countries, effective 12:01 a.m. EDT Aug 29, 2025, India included [FACT-dated; Federal Register 2025-16802; CBP fact sheet]. There is now NO de-minimis duty-free exemption for shipments from India: a direct parcel from Ludhiana must be entered and pays full MFN duty (16-32% by fibre) + the India surcharge, with no $800 shield. The zero-inventory ship-direct concept the original plan silently assumed no longer exists.

included: EO 14324 dated Aug 29 2025 ending <$800 de-minimis for all countries
every India parcel now dutiable with no shield
the death of the zero-inventory ship-direct concept
excluded: the fee structure that reinforces it (MPF_HMF_FEES)

pros.claim: Dating the repeal precisely turns a vague 'tariffs changed' worry into a binding, citeable model-flip
pros.example: pinning Aug 29 2025 lets the brand reject any plan that still assumes duty-free parcels

cons.claim: A dated executive action can be amended or litigated, so the rule is firm now but not guaranteed permanent
cons.example: a future carve-out could partially restore a low-value lane, though none exists today

failure_modes: modelling any ship-direct-per-order economics as if the <$800 shield still applied
treating the repeal as a marginal cost rather than a model-flip
acceptance_tests: EO 14324 effective Aug 29 2025 ending the <$800 duty-free exemption for all countries including India is stated as [FACT-dated], with every parcel now dutiable
revisit_triggers: the EO is amended, litigated or partially reversed
a low-value-import carve-out is introduced
CBP issues new de-minimis guidance

base.update_signal: a de-minimis rule or EO 14324 status changes

nodes.definition: Model the most movable input: since 2025 the US layers a country-specific surcharge additively on top of MFN for India (total duty ~= MFN base + India surcharge, both on entered value) [FACT-additive stacking]. It is fibre-blind, so it raises the whole stack equally and does not change the A1-vs-A2 ranking (the 32% MMF base already did that). History: 25% reciprocal (Apr 2025), +25% penal to a 50% peak (Aug 2025, realised and held ~5 months), interim cut to 18% (~Feb 2026), then ~10% Section 122 after the IEEPA basis was struck (~Feb 2026). Current ~10% [FACT], under appeal, statutorily sunsets ~Jul 24 2026 (Section 122 caps at 150 days). Model as a 0-15% band central ~10%; the forward level is a genuine [UNKNOWN] with a pending Section-301 risk.

included: the additive-on-MFN mechanism and fibre-blindness
the ~10% current [FACT] baseline and the realised 50% peak [FACT]
the [UNKNOWN] forward with the ~Jul-2026 sunset and Section-301 risk

pros.claim: Modelling the surcharge as a band plus a labelled forward [UNKNOWN] avoids hardening a single volatile number into a false forecast
pros.example: carrying central ~10% with a 0-15% band lets the brand re-confirm per PO instead of betting on one rate

cons.claim: A band central ~10% can lull planning into ignoring that a 50% peak already happened and held for months
cons.example: a model anchored on 10% understates the realised tail risk the August-2025 spike proved

failure_modes: hardening the ~10% current rate into a forward forecast despite the [UNKNOWN] tag
forgetting the surcharge is additive and applying it multiplicatively on the MFN-inclusive value
acceptance_tests: the additive mechanism, current ~10% [FACT], realised 50% peak [FACT], the [UNKNOWN] forward, the ~Jul-2026 sunset and the Section-301 risk are all stated with the 0-15% central-~10% band
revisit_triggers: a new surcharge action or rate change is announced
the Section-122 baseline sunsets ~Jul 2026
the Section-301 investigation on India concludes

base.update_signal: an India surcharge rate, sunset, or 301 outcome changes

nodes.definition: Establish that the blend ratio is a tariff switch, not a soft spec. Classification is by fibre of chief weight by mass: a 55% cotton / 45% acrylic A1 garment is 'cotton' at ~16.5%, but flip to 55% acrylic and the same sweater becomes MMF at ~32% - its duty nearly doubles [FACT-chief-weight rule]. As Importer of Record the brand owns this liability: a supplier quietly under-blending to cut yarn cost can push a 'cotton-blend' past 50% MMF and leave the brand mis-declaring duty. Blend % + tolerance + a fibre-composition / duty-classification check must be written into every PO [FACT-chief-weight rule + IOR liability; ESTIMATE-drift risk].

included: chief-weight-by-mass flipping 16.5% to 32% across the 50% line
the brand-as-IOR mis-declaration liability
the blend %+tolerance+fibre-check PO control

pros.claim: Treating the blend ratio as a duty switch turns a quality spec into a hard compliance control the brand can enforce
pros.example: a PO clause fixing 55/45 cotton ± tolerance with a fibre-composition test prevents a silent slide into the 32% MMF line

cons.claim: Drift risk magnitude is an [ESTIMATE], so the control is mandatory but the realised exposure is uncertain
cons.example: a reliable supplier may never drift, making the test a cheap insurance against an uncertain event

failure_modes: omitting blend %+tolerance from the PO and discovering a mis-declared MMF garment at audit
assuming a 'cotton-blend' label fixes the duty line when chief weight by mass actually governs
acceptance_tests: the chief-weight rule flipping 16.5% to 32% across the 50% line, the IOR mis-declaration liability and the blend %+tolerance+fibre-check PO control are all stated
revisit_triggers: a supplier blend-composition test comes back off-tolerance
a CBP audit or ruling addresses a blend classification
the cotton-vs-MMF duty spread widens, raising the stakes of a drift

base.update_signal: a blend-composition result, audit, or duty-spread change occurs

nodes.definition: Model inbound freight as a volume curve, not a number, India (Nhava Sheva/Mundra) to LA/Oakland 2026 [FACT-rate bands]: ocean FCL (40ft) ~$3,500-7,800/container (~5,000-10,000 sweaters) = ~$0.5-1.5/garment, the right answer at maturity/bulk; ocean LCL ~$30-180/CBM + ~$150-300 fixed CFS/doc/ISF = ~$1-6/garment + fixed drag, the first small bulk runs; air consolidated ~$5-8/kg (a sweater ~0.3-0.5 kg) = ~$1.5-4/garment for samples/urgent restock only; air express courier ~$8-12/kg = ~$3-6 + parcel fees, samples/PPS only never bulk. Plan launch at ~$1.5-3.5/unit (first LCL) and maturity at ~$0.5-1.5/unit (FCL) [ESTIMATE, MED - a curve not a point]. The per-order air-from-India route is ~$3-6/garment of freight alone before any duty.

included: FCL/LCL/air per-garment freight bands as a volume curve
launch-LCL vs maturity-FCL planning points
air-per-order as the dead de-minimis route
excluded: MPF/HMF and broker fees (separate fee nodes)

pros.claim: Presenting freight as a step-down curve stops a single freight number from mis-pricing either launch or maturity
pros.example: modelling LCL ~$2.5 at launch and FCL ~$1 at maturity prices the brand's actual trajectory rather than one point

cons.claim: The curve is rate-band-only until a live forwarder quote lands, so per-unit freight stays an [ESTIMATE] band
cons.example: a real FCL+drayage+3PL-receiving quote could shift the maturity point inside the band

failure_modes: hardening one freight figure and mis-pricing the launch LCL run or the mature FCL run
modelling air-per-order freight as if it were a viable bulk mode
acceptance_tests: the FCL/LCL/air per-garment bands, the launch-LCL and maturity-FCL planning points and the air-per-order dead-route flag are all stated as a labelled curve
revisit_triggers: a live forwarder quote for FCL/LCL + drayage + 3PL receiving lands
ocean or air rate bands shift materially
the brand's per-shipment volume crosses an FCL threshold

base.update_signal: a freight rate band or a live forwarder quote changes

nodes.definition: State the per-entry federal fee lines and why they reward bulk: MPF (FY2026) is 0.3464% of entered value with a $33.58 minimum / $651.50 maximum per formal entry [FACT-CBP]. The $651.50 cap is the whole story - a $50k bulk entry hits the cap at ~$0.13-0.65/garment over 1,000-5,000 pieces, while a single ship-direct parcel pays the $33.58 floor on one garment, murderous per unit. HMF is 0.125% of cargo value, ocean only, no cap [FACT] - ~$0.006 on a $5 sweater, trivial, and air is HMF-exempt. The fee structure alone, before a cent of duty, rewards bulk and punishes per-order, which is what makes the de-minimis death a clean model-flip rather than a marginal cost.

included: MPF 0.3464% with $33.58 floor / $651.50 cap
HMF 0.125% ocean-only no-cap
the cap as the bulk-vs-per-order driver

pros.claim: The MPF cap makes the bulk-vs-per-order case on fees alone, independent of duty
pros.example: one bulk entry capping at $651.50 over thousands of pieces versus a $33.58 floor per single parcel proves the model-flip on fees

cons.claim: The fees are small per garment at bulk, so over-focusing on them distracts from the dominant duty and freight lines
cons.example: shaving MPF is trivial next to a 32% MMF duty swing on A2

failure_modes: paying the MPF floor repeatedly via many tiny entries instead of capping it on one bulk entry
forgetting HMF is ocean-only and mis-applying it to an air entry
acceptance_tests: MPF 0.3464% with the $33.58 floor and $651.50 cap and HMF 0.125% ocean-only no-cap are stated, with the cap flagged as the bulk-vs-per-order driver
revisit_triggers: CBP revises the MPF rate, floor or cap for a new fiscal year
the HMF rate changes
the brand's entry value crosses the MPF cap threshold

base.update_signal: an MPF or HMF rate, floor or cap changes

nodes.definition: State the remaining import-chain cost lines and their per-unit behaviour: customs broker entry ~$150-400/entry + ISF ~$35-75; continuous bond ~$400-1,200/yr (beats single-entry above ~3 shipments/yr) or single-entry ~$75-275; Importer-of-Record setup ~$50-150 one-time [FACT-2026 broker reportage]; plus drayage / last-mile to the CA 3PL. Amortised over a bulk entry these are ~$0.10-0.80/garment; they become dominant per-unit only if you do many tiny entries (the ship-direct model again). Like MPF/HMF, the entry-cost structure rewards bulk and punishes per-order.

included: broker entry, ISF, continuous-vs-single-entry bond, IOR setup and drayage
amortised ~$0.10-0.80/garment at bulk
continuous bond breakeven above ~3 entries/yr

pros.claim: Itemising entry costs and their bulk amortisation shows they vanish per-unit at bulk and only bite under the dead ship-direct model
pros.example: a continuous bond plus one brokered bulk entry spreading to ~$0.30/garment versus a broker fee per tiny parcel

cons.claim: These bands are 2026 reportage, so the exact per-entry figure varies by broker and shipment cadence

edges.resolution_rule: choose bulk ocean to a 3PL: post-de-minimis every parcel is dutiable and the MPF floor + per-entry costs make air-per-order uneconomic despite its speed; reserve air for samples/PPS only

edges.why_related: the [UNKNOWN]-knit+LINK ex-factory width caps how tight any landed band can be
running the stack at the 25-50% spike feeds the realised landed-duty figures back to widen the planning range
the 32% MMF rate causally drives the border re-ranking of the line

conflict_axes.name: factory_gate_vs_landed_ranking
conflict_axes.description: The ex-factory view ranks A2 acrylic cheapest (A2<A1<A3) while the landed view ranks it level with cotton (A1~=A2<A3); a single ranking misleads.
poles: lead on the factory-gate cost ranking
lead on the landed cost ranking
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: report both views distinctly and lead downstream with the landed A1~=A2<A3, since the 32% MMF duty erases acrylic's ex-factory lead at the border

conflict_axes.name: firm_mfn_base_vs_volatile_surcharge
conflict_axes.description: The MFN trio is a firm [FACT] anchor while the additive India surcharge is a volatile band whose forward level is [UNKNOWN]; either can be over-weighted in an all-in duty number.
poles: anchor on the firm MFN rates
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the MFN trio as the citeable anchor that sets fibre ranking and carry the surcharge as a 0-15% central-~10% band plus a 25-50% spike scenario, re-confirmed per PO

conflict_axes.name: ship_direct_speed_vs_bulk_fee_economics
conflict_axes.description: Air ship-direct is fast but, post-de-minimis, pays full duty + MPF floor + per-entry costs per parcel, while bulk ocean is slow but caps MPF and amortises freight and entry costs.
poles: ship direct per order for speed
bulk import to a 3PL for cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to bulk IOR to a CA 3PL with domestic ship; reserve air only for samples/PPS, because the dead de-minimis makes per-order air uneconomic

conflict_axes.name: per_unit_landed_profit_vs_cash_cycle
conflict_axes.description: A garment can be profitable per landed unit yet die on the months-long cash-out of bulk inventory, so per-order viability is necessary but not sufficient.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat per-order landed profitability as necessary-not-sufficient and require the working-capital cycle to be funded before the first bulk PO

conflict_axes.name: blend_yarn_saving_vs_duty_cliff
conflict_axes.description: Under-blending toward more acrylic cuts yarn cost but, past 50% chief weight, flips a 'cotton' garment to the 32% MMF line and the brand-as-IOR mis-declares.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fix blend % +/- tolerance with a fibre-composition check in every PO; a small yarn saving is not worth a near-doubled duty and a mis-declaration liability

conflict_axes.name: single_point_cogs_vs_honest_band
conflict_axes.description: Stakeholders want one COGS number per article while the evidence supports only a band whose width comes from the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate and the volatile surcharge.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry the band and label any single-point figure a [DOWNGRADED] band-centre illustration robust in direction and soft in level

conflict_axes.name: central_10pct_planning_vs_50pct_tail
conflict_axes.description: Planning on the central ~10% surcharge is convenient but a 50% peak already happened and held ~5 months, so the realised tail must be stress-tested.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: plan central ~10% but require survival of a 25-50% spike at the bulk-PO window given the realised Aug-2025 peak and the ~Jul-2026 sunset + 301 risk

conflict_axes.name: duty_friendly_cotton_vs_premium_carrying_a3
conflict_axes.description: Cotton (A1) is the duty-and-cost-friendly anchor while merino (A3) is the dearest landed yet the article that carries the line; the friendly article and the load-bearing article differ.
poles: anchor the line on duty-friendly cotton
lead the line on premium merino
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use A1 as the friendly core and treat A3 as the load-bearing but [ESTIMATE, LOW] band needing an importer quote before any margin use

edge_cases.description: A supplier under-blends a 'cotton' garment past 50% acrylic, flipping it to the 32% MMF line and making the brand-as-IOR mis-declare duty
edge_cases.trigger: a chief-weight blend drift past the 50% line without a fibre-composition check
edge_cases.mitigation: write blend % +/- tolerance + a fibre-composition / duty-classification check into every PO and test on receipt

edge_cases.description: The India surcharge returns to the realised 25-50% peak at the first bulk-PO window, swinging landed COGS 50%+
edge_cases.trigger: the Section-122 baseline sunsets ~Jul 2026 or a Section-301 tariff replaces it during the launch window
edge_cases.mitigation: re-confirm the surcharge before committing the bulk PO and stress-test contribution at A1 ~66.5% / A2 ~82% / A3 ~66% total duty

edge_cases.description: A ship-direct-per-order plan is modelled as if the <$800 de-minimis shield still applied after Aug 29 2025
edge_cases.trigger: an import plan assumes duty-free low-value parcels post-EO-14324
edge_cases.mitigation: switch to bulk IOR to a CA 3PL; every parcel is now dutiable and the MPF floor punishes per-order

edge_cases.description: An upstream margin model still uses the corrected-away 'cotton ~7%' duty figure
edge_cases.trigger: a downstream P&L inherits the discredited ~7% cotton rate instead of ~16.5%
edge_cases.mitigation: correct every model up to the ~16.5% cotton rate (6110.20.20); the ~7% figure is a known error

edge_cases.description: A band-centre landed point ($11/$11/$20) is quoted as a measured COGS rather than a [DOWNGRADED] illustration
edge_cases.trigger: a single-point figure is read as a fact despite the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK width
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the band and label the point a band-centre illustration robust in direction, soft in level

edge_cases.description: Freight is multiplied by the duty rate or included in the dutiable base
edge_cases.trigger: the landed formula treats freight as part of the transaction value
edge_cases.mitigation: compute duty on the ex-factory transaction value only and add separately-stated freight after duty

edge_cases.description: The MPF floor is paid repeatedly via many tiny entries instead of capping at $651.50 on one bulk entry
edge_cases.trigger: a per-order or fragmented-entry import pattern
edge_cases.mitigation: consolidate into bulk entries to hit the MPF cap and amortise broker/bond/ISF costs

edge_cases.description: A3 merino's band-centre ~$20 is used in a margin model before an importer quotes the premium tops
edge_cases.trigger: the [ESTIMATE, LOW] yarn-dominated A3 band is treated as margin-usable
edge_cases.mitigation: get an importer merino/lambswool quote before any A3 margin use; A3 carries the line so its COGS must be load-bearing

edge_cases.description: The bulk model is adopted without funding the months-long inventory cash-out, so a per-order-profitable brand dies on cash timing
edge_cases.trigger: a bulk PO is committed before the working-capital cycle is funded
edge_cases.mitigation: fund the dye-lot MOQ + ocean lead-time + refund cycle before the first bulk PO; per-order viability is necessary not sufficient

edge_cases.description: An athlete/celebrity name or likeness is printed on a sweater on the assumption that 'AI-designed' launders the right of publicity
edge_cases.trigger: a design or creator campaign uses a recognizable living or deceased person without a license
edge_cases.mitigation: clear marks/likenesses before any print or post; California protects living and deceased persons and damages include the infringer's profits

edge_cases.description: A continuous bond is skipped past ~3 entries/yr, paying single-entry bonds where a continuous bond is cheaper
edge_cases.trigger: the brand runs more than ~3 entries/yr on single-entry bonds
edge_cases.mitigation: switch to a continuous bond once entry cadence exceeds ~3/yr

edge_cases.description: The fibre-blind surcharge is assumed to re-rank the A1-vs-A2 line
edge_cases.trigger: a model lets the surcharge change the fibre ordering it cannot affect
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the surcharge as fibre-blind (raises the whole stack equally); only the 32% MMF base re-ranks the line

workflow.action: Accept the T4 ex-factory bands as input
workflow.description: State A1 ~$4-9, A2 ~$3.5-8, A3 ~$6-22+ as accepted [ESTIMATE] input with the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate as the width driver
workflow.gate: the three ex-factory bands are stated as accepted input with the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK width driver named

workflow.description: Map A1/A2/A3 to 6110.20.20 / 6110.30.30 / 6110.11.00 by chief weight, noting no India FTA preference
workflow.gate: the three fibre sub-lines and chief-weight-by-mass classifier are stated with the no-India-preference fact

workflow.action: Fix the correct MFN duty trio
workflow.description: State cotton ~16.5% / wool ~16% / acrylic-MMF ~32% as [FACT-USITC] with the ~7% correction and the MMF wall
workflow.gate: the corrected 16.5/16/32 trio is stated [FACT] with the ~7% cotton error rejected

workflow.action: Establish the de-minimis repeal and bulk-import model
workflow.description: State EO 14324 (Aug 29 2025) and derive the bulk IOR to CA 3PL to domestic-ship default
workflow.gate: the dated repeal and the bulk-import model-flip are stated

workflow.description: State the additive mechanism, current ~10% [FACT], realised 50% peak [FACT] and [UNKNOWN] forward with the 0-15% central-~10% band
workflow.gate: the additive mechanism, ~10% current, 50% peak and [UNKNOWN] forward are stated as a band

workflow.action: Add the freight curve and fee lines
workflow.description: State MPF/HMF, broker/bond/drayage and the freight curve, all rewarding bulk over per-order
workflow.gate: MPF/HMF, broker/bond/drayage and the freight curve are stated with the bulk-vs-per-order driver

workflow.action: Stack the duty and landed formulas
workflow.description: Recompute duty $ = ex-factory x (MFN+surcharge) and landed = ex-factory x (1+MFN+surcharge) + freight + fees
workflow.gate: both formulas are stated and recompute the A1/A2/A3 landed bands at central ~10%

workflow.description: Show factory-gate A2<A1<A3 inverting to landed A1~=A2<A3 with cotton as the duty-friendly anchor
workflow.gate: the inversion, the dollar mechanism and cotton-as-anchor are stated

workflow.action: Produce the three per-article landed bands
workflow.description: State A1 ~$6-14, A2 ~$6-14, A3 ~$9-31+ with rates, surcharge, freight/fees and band-centre [DOWNGRADED] points
workflow.gate: each article's band states its rate, surcharge, freight/fees and [DOWNGRADED] band-centre

workflow.description: Re-run the stack at 25-50% to give A1 ~66.5% / A2 ~82% / A3 ~66% total duty and the sunset/301 launch-window risk
workflow.gate: the 25-50% spike landed-duty figures and the ~Jul-2026 sunset + 301 risk are stated

workflow.action: Carry the working-capital and legal flags
workflow.description: Name the bulk-inventory cash trap and the IOR/right-of-publicity legal flags as binding, not added per-unit
workflow.gate: the cash-cycle trap and both legal flags are stated as binding conditions

workflow.description: Deliver per-article landed COGS-to-stock with the surcharge stress range and the binding PO/operating conditions, stopping before CAC/contribution
workflow.gate: the per-article landed bands, the stress range, the clean pre-CAC boundary and the four binding conditions are stated

dominance_rules.rule: The corrected MFN trio dominates any legacy cotton-duty figure
dominance_rules.rationale: the cotton sweater rate is ~16.5% (6110.20.20), not the corrected-away ~7%
dominance_rules.trigger: any model attaches a cotton sweater duty below ~16.5%
dominance_rules.action: replace it with ~16.5% and flag the ~7% as a known upstream error

dominance_rules.rule: The landed ranking dominates the factory-gate ranking downstream
dominance_rules.rationale: the 32% MMF duty erases acrylic's ex-factory cost lead at the border
dominance_rules.trigger: a downstream decision leads on the factory-gate A2<A1<A3 ordering
dominance_rules.action: lead with the landed A1~=A2<A3 ranking and treat acrylic as not cheaper than cotton

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty band dominates any single-point landed COGS
dominance_rules.rationale: the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate and the volatile surcharge make a point figure unsupportable
dominance_rules.trigger: a single landed COGS point is quoted as measured
dominance_rules.action: carry the band and label the point a [DOWNGRADED] band-centre illustration

dominance_rules.rule: Bulk import dominates ship-direct after the de-minimis repeal
dominance_rules.rationale: every parcel is now dutiable and the MPF floor + per-entry costs punish per-order
dominance_rules.trigger: an import plan proposes ship-direct per order
dominance_rules.action: default to bulk IOR to a CA 3PL with domestic ship; reserve air for samples only

dominance_rules.rule: Duty applies to the ex-factory value, not the freight-inflated value
dominance_rules.rationale: US apparel entries use transaction value with separately-stated freight excluded
dominance_rules.trigger: a duty calc includes freight in the dutiable base
dominance_rules.action: compute duty on the ex-factory transaction value and add freight after duty

dominance_rules.rule: The chief-weight cliff dominates a marginal yarn saving
dominance_rules.rationale: drifting past 50% MMF nearly doubles duty and creates IOR mis-declaration liability
dominance_rules.trigger: a blend is shifted toward more acrylic to cut yarn cost
dominance_rules.action: hold blend % +/- tolerance with a fibre-composition check; the duty cliff outweighs the saving

dominance_rules.rule: The realised 50% spike dominates central-only surcharge planning
dominance_rules.rationale: the 50% peak happened and held ~5 months, with a ~Jul-2026 sunset and 301 risk on the launch window
dominance_rules.trigger: a bulk PO is planned on the central ~10% alone
dominance_rules.action: stress-test 25-50% and re-confirm the surcharge before committing the PO

dominance_rules.rule: Cash-cycle survival dominates per-order landed profitability
dominance_rules.rationale: a per-order-profitable brand can still die on the months-long bulk-inventory cash-out
dominance_rules.trigger: a go decision rests on per-unit landed margin alone
dominance_rules.action: require the working-capital cycle to be funded before the first bulk PO

anti_rework_rules.rule: Use the corrected ~16.5% cotton duty from the first model, never ~7%
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a downstream P&L built on the discredited cotton rate that must later be corrected up

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry the surcharge as a band plus a 25-50% spike scenario from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: hardening a single volatile surcharge into a forecast that a sunset or 301 action invalidates

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute duty on the ex-factory value and add freight after, in the same step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a freight-inflated dutiable base that overstates duty and must be re-derived

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every single-point landed figure a [DOWNGRADED] band-centre illustration when first produced
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a band-centre point circulating as a measured COGS and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write blend % +/- tolerance + a fibre-composition check into every PO
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a chief-weight drift into the 32% MMF line and an IOR mis-declaration discovered at audit

anti_rework_rules.rule: Default to bulk IOR to a CA 3PL and reserve air for samples before pricing freight
anti_rework_rules.prevents: pricing a dead ship-direct model and re-routing the whole import chain after the fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Get an importer merino quote before using A3 in any margin model
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the line-carrying A3 band hardening on a stale yarn anchor and breaking the contribution math later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the working-capital cash trap as a cash-cycle cost, not a per-unit COGS add, from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: double-counting the inverted-duty/GST drag in COGS or omitting the cash-timing kill-risk entirely

iteration_protocol.trigger: a live Ludhiana knit+LINK job-work quote lands
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the ex-factory input and re-run every landed band, halving the band width

iteration_protocol.trigger: the India surcharge changes, sunsets ~Jul 2026, or the Section-301 investigation concludes
iteration_protocol.action: update the surcharge band and spike scenario and re-confirm the all-in duty per article

iteration_protocol.trigger: an importer quotes the premium merino/lambswool tops
iteration_protocol.action: replace the stale A3 yarn anchor and re-band A3 landed before any margin use

iteration_protocol.trigger: a live forwarder quote for FCL/LCL + drayage + 3PL receiving lands
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the freight curve from a band to a point and re-run the landed stack

iteration_protocol.trigger: a USITC MFN rate change or a CBP classification ruling lands
iteration_protocol.action: update the duty trio and re-run the duty and landed formulas and the re-ranking

iteration_protocol.trigger: a de-minimis carve-out or a CBP MPF/bond fee schedule change lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the bulk-import model and the fee lines

iteration_protocol.trigger: the dye-lot MOQ, ocean lead time or inverted-duty/GST refund cycle is measured at a named vendor
iteration_protocol.action: quantify the working-capital trap and update the hand-off conditions

priority_rationale: The ex-factory input, HTS classification, MFN duty trio, de-minimis repeal and India surcharge come first because every landed number depends on the correct fibre rate, the additive surcharge and the post-de-minimis import model; the chief-weight cliff, freight curve and MPF/HMF/broker fees next, because they are the cost lines and compliance switches the stack adds; the duty and landed formulas then recompute the bands and the border re-ranking; the three per-article bands and the surcharge spike apply the formulas to concrete articles and stress them; and the working-capital, legal, honesty and hand-off nodes come last because they compose the landed COGS-to-stock output, its binding conditions and its clean boundary before the demand-side contribution P&L.
